title: The ordinary Koszul limit includes quasi-isomorphically into its explicit Roos fibre
statement: Let C be a small category with Grothendieck topology J, O a sheaf of commutative rings, r any natural number, and b a Fin r-indexed family of global sections. Let I be a K-injective complex of O-module sheaves. Form the actual strict tensor tower X=ringedKoszulTensorTowerComplex O r b I of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system]. Using the explicit ordinary-limit inclusion ExactProductsRoos.comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-products-roos-comparison], the chain map lim X → mappingCocone(-(1-shift):product X→product X) with zero second coordinate is a quasi-isomorphism. There is no hypothesis of exact countable products, no derived-category parameter and no termwise injectivity assumption on I. This is a statement only about ordinary complexes.

source.place: Tag 0A0A, lemma-colim-and-lim-of-duals; derived.tex Tag 0949, lemma-colim-hocolim; the ordinary Hom/telescope calculation preceding the derived comparison

proof.text: Obtain f and its two canonicality equations and quasi-isomorphism from quasiIso_telescopeColimit. Apply quasiIso_homComplex_map to the identity of the K-injective I and f; the identity coefficient map simplifies away.

Use exists_ringedKoszul_finiteHomTower_iso to identify the entire inverse Hom diagram with the actual strict tensor tower, including its transitions. Apply telescopeHom_roos_arrow_iso to this tower isomorphism and both canonicality equations of f.
Transport the quasi-isomorphism of Hom(f,I) across the isomorphism of arrows using quasiIso_iff_of_arrow_mk_iso.

proof_origin.note: J4 writes the complete K-injective quasi-isomorphism assembly. The two remaining algebraic steps are strictly smaller: finite evaluation of the whole tower, and a general telescope-Hom arrow isomorphism without quasi-isomorphism hypotheses or conclusions.

mathlib_searches.query: An internal Hom functor sends sequential homotopy colimits to inverse homotopy limits
mathlib_searches.results: 8 hits, including ihom, internalHom and colimitHomIsoLimitYoneda. These provide adjunction/universal-property tools but not the signed chain-level strict Koszul-to-Roos map.

mathlib_searches.query: The ordinary to derived inverse limit comparison is an isomorphism for a Koszul Hom tower of K-injective coefficients
mathlib_searches.results: 8 hits, including injective-resolution and degree-zero right-derived comparisons. None states the ordinary-complex Koszul telescope/Roos identification.

Searched Mathlib through msearch and rg on lean/Sheaf and lean/WeilConjectures. Existing exact-product Roos descent has a stronger exact-product assumption. HomComplexMappingCone treats the second Hom variable. RingedKoszulColimitHomOrdinaryLimit supplies the ordinary limit isomorphism but no telescope-fibre identification.
